passages.text: On the next day, then, Peter, who was about to debate with Simon, woke rather early and prayed. Just as he finished, Zacchaeus came in and said, “Simon is sitting outside, speaking with some of his own people, about thirty of them.” Peter said, “Let him speak until a crowd gathers, and then let us begin the debate. In this way we can hear what he says, prepare ourselves to address it, and go out and speak.” And that is what happened. Zacchaeus went out and, not long afterward, came back in and reported to Peter the statements Simon had made against Peter.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀντέβαλλεν τῷ Πέτρῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: reported to Peter
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb can denote comparison or putting statements before someone; reported fits the messenger’s relay of Simon’s speech, not a second debate with Peter.

passages.text: He said, “He accuses you, Peter, of being a servant of evil, of having great power in magic, and of filling people’s souls with images in a way worse than idolatry. He seemed to offer this as proof that you are a magician, saying: ‘I know about myself that I think things through when I am alone, but when I come to debate with him, I do not remember a single argument. For while he is speaking, my mind is occupied with recalling the things I had thought of saying to him when I came, and I do not hear anything at all that he says. Since I do not experience anything like this with anyone else, but only with him, how am I not being bewitched by him? That whatever he teaches is worse than idolatry will be clear to anyone with understanding once I explain it. For there is no other benefit than for the soul to become free of idols of every kind. When it imagines a form, it is bound by fear; it withers with anxiety about suffering something, and, being altered, becomes possessed. Yet in its possession it seems to most people to be sound-minded.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κακίας ὄντα ὑπηρέτην
lexical_decisions.chosen: being a servant of evil
lexical_decisions.rationale: This is Simon’s reported accusation, not the narrator’s verdict. ὑπηρέτης is an assistant or subordinate.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: φαντασιοῦντα
lexical_decisions.chosen: filling ... with images
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the mental-image vocabulary that structures Simon’s criticism, not generic deception alone.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰδώλων παντοδα[πῶν]
lexical_decisions.chosen: idols of every kind
lexical_decisions.rationale: The bracketed letters already belong to the supplied edition’s reading. No new restoration is made.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δαιμονοῦσα
lexical_decisions.chosen: in its possession
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the demon/possession language; raves or acts like one possessed is a possible phenomenological rendering.

passages.text: This is what Peter gives you under a promise of making you sound-minded. For under the pretext of one God he seems to free you from many lifeless idols. These do not do their worshipers much harm, because with their very eyes they can see that they are stone, bronze, gold, or some other lifeless material. Therefore, knowing that what is seen is nothing, the soul cannot be haunted by fear in the same way through the visible thing. But when, through deceptive teaching, it looks toward a fearsome God, it is uprooted from its natural condition. I say these things not because I advise you to revere idols, but because Peter, while seeming to free your souls from fearsome ideas, makes each of your minds possessed by a more fearsome idea, introducing a God with a form—and, moreover, supremely just. With this comes terror, and shuddering for the soul that thinks of it, capable even of loosening the tension of sound reasoning. For the mind, placed in such a storm, has its brightness muddied like deep water by a violent wind. Therefore, if he comes for your benefit, let him not, while seeming to dissolve your relatively mild fears arising from lifeless forms, introduce in their place a fearsome form of God. But does God have a form? If he does, he has a shape. If he has a shape, how is he not bounded? If bounded, he is in a place. If in a place, he is less than the place containing him. If less than something, how is he greater, stronger, or higher than all? So much for these matters.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς φοβερὸν θεὸν ἀποβλέπουσα τῶν κατὰ φύσιν ἐκβαθρεύεται.
lexical_decisions.chosen: when ... it looks toward a fearsome God, it is uprooted from its natural condition
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the upheaval/derangement image and the author’s contrast with nature; this remains Simon’s reported position.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν ὀρθῶν λογισμῶν ἐκλῦσαι τοὺς τόνους
lexical_decisions.chosen: loosening the tension of sound reasoning
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the tension image rather than merely saying it makes thinking difficult.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μορφὴν δὲ ἔχει θεός;
lexical_decisions.chosen: form ... shape ... bounded
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps distinct vocabulary in the chain of argument. Bounded denotes spatial delimitation, not simply weakness.

passages.text: It is also obvious that he does not truly believe even the things said by his own teacher, for he proclaims the opposite of them. For, as I learn, his teacher said to someone, “Do not call me good, for the good one is one.” In saying good, he does not mean that just one whom the scriptures proclaim, who kills and gives life—kills those who sin and gives life to those who live according to his judgment. That he really did not call the maker good is clear to anyone able to think it through. For the maker was known to Adam, whom he formed; to Enoch, who pleased him; to Noah, whom he saw to be righteous; likewise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and also to Moses, the people, and the whole world. Yet Peter’s teacher Jesus came and said, “No one knew the Father except the Son, just as no one knows the Son except the Father, and those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.” Therefore, if the one present was himself the Son, from his coming he revealed to those he wished the one unknown to all. Thus the Father was unknown to everyone before him, not being this one who was known to all.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μή με λέγε ἀγαθόν, ὁ γὰρ ἀγαθὸς εἷς ἐστίν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Do not call me good, for the good one is one
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the wording actually quoted here, not a familiar expanded Gospel form. Simon’s distinction between good and just is retained as his argument.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δημιουργοῦ
lexical_decisions.chosen: the maker
lexical_decisions.rationale: δημιουργός denotes creator or maker, not automatically an evil demiurge; the speaker’s proposed distinction is not editorially endorsed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ δικαίῳ ὁραθέντι Νῶε
lexical_decisions.chosen: Noah, whom he saw to be righteous
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes Noah as the one seen as righteous by God; it is not inverted into Noah seeing God.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα, εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱός, ὡς οὐδὲ τὸν υἱόν τις οἶδεν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατήρ
lexical_decisions.chosen: No one knew the Father except the Son, just as no one knows the Son except the Father
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the distinct Greek knew/knows forms instead of homogenizing the quoted tenses.

passages.text: And in saying this, Jesus does not even agree with himself. For sometimes, in other statements drawn from the scriptures, he establishes a fearsome and just God, saying, “Do not fear the one who kills the body but can do nothing to the soul. Fear the one who can cast both body and soul into the Gehenna of fire. Yes, I tell you, fear this one.” That he really said to fear this one as a just God, to whom he also says the wronged should cry out, is shown when he gives a parable on this and adds its explanation, saying, “If, then, the unjust judge acted in this way because he was petitioned repeatedly, how much more will the Father bring vindication for those who cry to him day and night? Or do you think that because he is patient with them, he will not do it? Yes, I tell you, he will do it, and quickly.” But whoever says that God vindicates and repays establishes him as just by nature, and not good. Further, he also gives thanks to the Lord of heaven and earth. If he is Lord of heaven and earth, he is acknowledged as maker; and being maker, he is just. Calling him good at one time and just at another, he does not agree even in this way. Thirdly, his wise disciple insisted yesterday that direct perception is more adequate than an apparition, not knowing that direct perception can be human, whereas an apparition is acknowledged to belong to divinity.’

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρὸς
lexical_decisions.chosen: the Gehenna of fire
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the named place and fire qualification, not the distinct Hades term.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν ἐκδίκησιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: vindication
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐκδίκησις can be vengeance or the securing of justice. Vindication fits the wronged petitioners while retaining the punitive repayment explained afterward.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐνάργειαν ὀπτασίας ἱκανωτέραν εἶναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: direct perception is more adequate than an apparition
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐνάργεια here is direct evident encounter, contrasted with ὀπτασία, an apparition. The polemical wise disciple is not softened into neutral description.

passages.text: “By these and similar statements, Peter, Simon, standing outside and speaking to the crowds, seems to me to be disturbing most of them. So go out immediately and dissolve his false arguments by the power of truth.” After Zacchaeus said this, Peter prayed as usual and went out. He stood in the place of the previous day, greeted the crowds in the customary manner of reverence toward God, and began to speak as follows: “Our Lord Jesus, being a true prophet—as I will also give assurance about this at the proper time—made concise declarations about matters important to the truth, for these two reasons. First, he addressed people who revered God and knew to believe what he uttered as a declaration, for what was said was not foreign to their customary practice. Second, because he had a limited time to proclaim, he did not employ demonstrative argument, so that he might not spend all his allotted time on arguments. Otherwise he would have been occupied with explaining a few statements that could be understood through effort of soul, and would thus not have introduced the matters important to truth more extensively. For he declared what he wished as to a people able to understand, among whom we too belong. Whenever, on a rare occasion, we did not understand something he said, we asked him privately, so that none of what he said would remain unintelligible to us.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὸν πρὸ μιᾶς τόπον
lexical_decisions.chosen: in the place of the previous day
lexical_decisions.rationale: The elliptical before one refers to one day before; no new location is invented.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ τῆς ἀποδείξεως οὐκ ἐχρῆτο λόγῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: he did not employ demonstrative argument
lexical_decisions.rationale: Distinguishes concise pronouncement from developed proof, not truthful from untruthful speech.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν ὑπὸ πόνου ψυχῆς νοεῖσθαι δυναμένων
lexical_decisions.chosen: that could be understood through effort of soul
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the intellectual effort supplied by the source rather than rendering the matters permanently incomprehensible.

passages.text: Knowing, then, that we knew everything he had said and could supply the proofs, when he sent us to the uninstructed nations to baptize them for forgiveness of sins, he commanded us to teach them first. Of these commands, this is the first and great one: to fear the Lord God and serve him alone. The God he said to fear is the one whose angels belonging to the least of the believers among us stand in heaven continually beholding the Father’s face. For he has a form for the sake of primary and sole beauty, and all his members, not for use. He does not have eyes in order to see from there, for he sees from every side, being in body incomparably brighter than the seeing spirit within us and more radiant than every light, so that compared with him the sun’s light is reckoned darkness. Nor does he have ears in order to hear, for from every side he hears, understands, moves, acts, and makes. He has the most beautiful form for the human being’s sake, so that the pure in heart may be able to see him and rejoice in that for which they endured these things. For with his form, as with a most magnificent seal, he stamped out the human being, so that the human being might rule and have dominion over all and everything might serve him. Therefore, having determined that the whole should be himself and the human being his image—he himself invisible, but his image, the human being, visible—the one who wishes to revere him honors his visible image, namely the human being. Whatever someone does to a human being, whether good or evil, is referred to him. Therefore judgment from him will go forth to all, assigning to each what is deserved, for it vindicates his form.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μορφὴν γὰρ ἔχει διὰ πρῶτον καὶ μόνον κάλλος
lexical_decisions.chosen: he has a form for the sake of primary and sole beauty
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the unusual first/only qualification of beauty. For beauty first and alone is another possible grouping, treating first adverbially; neither reading makes the form a merely metaphorical appearance.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: λαμπρότερος ὢν τὸ σῶμα
lexical_decisions.chosen: being in body ... brighter
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the author’s explicit bodily attribution to God without conforming it to a later account of divine incorporeality.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῇ γὰρ αὐτοῦ μορφῇ ὡς ἐν μεγίστῃ σφραγῖδι τὸν ἄνθρωπον διετυπώσατο
lexical_decisions.chosen: with his form, as with a most magnificent seal, he stamped out the human being
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the form/seal/imprint sequence and its relation to human dominion.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κρίνας εἶναι τὸ πᾶν αὐτὸν καὶ τὴν αὐτοῦ εἰκόνα τὸν ἄνθρωπον
lexical_decisions.chosen: having determined that the whole should be himself and the human being his image
lexical_decisions.rationale: The abstract the whole remains explicit. The exact relation of himself to the whole can be read as constitutive totality rather than an identity doctrine; the English does not supply a later metaphysical explanation.

passages.text: But someone will say, “If he has a form, he also has a shape and is in a place. If he is in a place and contained by it as something lesser, how is he great above all? And how can he be everywhere while having a shape?” To the person saying this, one can first say: those around Simon persuade people to believe such thoughts about him; but we know to be true the things attested by our Lord Jesus Christ. We are not obliged to provide you at a command with proofs that things are so. But first I will speak about place and God. Place is what does not exist, whereas God is what exists; and what does not exist cannot be compared with what exists. For how can place have existence, unless it is a second region, such as heaven, earth, water, air, or any other body, which would itself also fill the void? It is called void for this reason: because it is nothing. Nothing is a more suitable name for it. For what is the so-called void—some sort of vessel that contains nothing? Yet the vessel itself, being empty, is not itself place; rather, if it is a vessel, place is that in which the empty vessel itself is. For what exists must necessarily be in what is nothing. This is what I mean by what does not exist, which some call place: it is nothing. How can what is nothing be compared with what exists, except as opposites, so that what exists is not called place, but what does not exist is? But even if it is something, although many examples press to come forth from me as proof, I wish to use just one, to show that what contains is not invariably stronger than what is contained. The sun is a circular shape and is wholly contained by air, but it illuminates the air, heats it, and cuts through it. When the sun is absent from it, the air is enveloped in darkness, and wherever a part of it becomes bright, it grows cold as though dying. But at the sun’s rising it is illuminated again, and wherever it is warmed by the sun it is also adorned with greater beauty. The sun does these things by its presence, although its substance is bounded. What, then, still prevents God, as the maker and master of this and everything, from himself having shape, form, and beauty, while the presence proceeding from him extends infinitely?

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἀληθεῖς γινώσκομεν τὰς μαρτυρουμένας
lexical_decisions.chosen: we know to be true the things attested
lexical_decisions.rationale: The feminine plural has no expressed noun; things or statements attested expresses the ellipsis without adding an extra source claim.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ μὲν ὂν μὴ ᾖ, τὸ δὲ μὴ ὂν τόπος λέγηται
lexical_decisions.chosen: what exists is not called place, but what does not exist is
lexical_decisions.rationale: Understands place from the second clause as the predicate to the first, not an assertion that what exists ceases to exist.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ οὗ ἂν αὐτοῦ μέρους λαμπρὸν γένηται, ὡς νεκρούμενον ψύχεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: wherever a part of it becomes bright, it grows cold as though dying
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied wording says bright, not dark. The resulting physical description is puzzling, but the main text preserves that printed adjective rather than silently emending it to fit the argument. Its referent is understood as a part of the air.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ μετουσίαν ἀπείρως ἐκτεταμένην ἔχειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the presence proceeding from him extends infinitely
lexical_decisions.rationale: μετουσία can be presence, participation, or communicated influence. Presence preserves the analogy with the bounded sun’s effects without adding a second bodily substance.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ οὗ ἂν αὐτοῦ μέρους λαμπρὸν γένηται, ὡς νεκρούμενον ψύχεται
source_issues.issue: The wording associates becoming bright with cooling, which is puzzling in this analogy. Bright is nevertheless what the supplied text says; no emendation to dark has been made.

passages.text: There is therefore one true God, who sits presiding in a superior form, being twice the heart of what is above and below. From him, as from a center, a substance wells forth with vital, incorporeal power and passes through all things, together with stars and the things belonging only to heaven, air, water, earth, fire, and anything else that exists. It is infinite in height, unbounded in depth, immeasurable in breadth, extending in three directions to infinity the life-giving and intelligent nature proceeding from him. This reality that proceeds from him and is infinite on every side must therefore have as its heart the one who truly is above all in shape. Wherever he may be, he is in the middle, as in something infinite, being the boundary of the whole. Therefore the extensions, beginning from him, have a nature drawn from what is boundless. Of these, one takes its beginning from him and reaches into height above, another into depth below, another to the right, another to the left, another in front, and another behind. Looking toward these as a number equal on every side, he completes the world in six intervals of time, himself being rest and having the coming boundless age as an image, being beginning and end. For the six infinities terminate in him and receive from him their extension into infinity.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ ἄνω τε καὶ κάτω δὶς ὑπάρχων καρδία
lexical_decisions.chosen: being twice the heart of what is above and below
lexical_decisions.rationale: δὶς literally means twice. Its precise link to above and below is compressed; the main text retains twice rather than replacing it with an unprinted cosmological term.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: σὺν τε ἄστροις καὶ μόνοις οὐρανοῦ, ἀέρος, ὕδατος, γῆς, πυρὸς
lexical_decisions.chosen: together with stars and the things belonging only to heaven, air, water, earth, fire
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adjective μόνοις is taken substantivally with an implicit things, qualified by the following genitives. The phrase is syntactically compressed; the main text preserves its only restriction and the complete element list, without changing μόνοις to another conjectured word.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐσία ἄπειρος εἰς ὕψος, ἀπέραντος εἰς βάθος, ἀμέτρητος εἰς πλάτος
lexical_decisions.chosen: a substance ... infinite in height, unbounded in depth, immeasurable in breadth
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the three distinct spatial measures and their distinct adjectives.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀνάγκη εἶναι καρδίαν, ἔχον τὸν ὄντως ὑπὲρ πάντα ἐν σχήματι
lexical_decisions.chosen: must ... have as its heart the one who truly is above all in shape
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes εἶναι with ἔχον as a having construction, καρδίαν as what is had, and the person as its identifying complement. A more formally segmented rendering is must be a heart, containing the one, but the center-and-extensions argument favors having him as heart.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν ἐσόμενον ἄπειρον αἰῶνα εἰκόνα ἔχων
lexical_decisions.chosen: having the coming boundless age as an image
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the future age and image relationship without substituting an unprinted doctrine of the seventh day.

source_issues.source_quote: σὺν τε ἄστροις καὶ μόνοις οὐρανοῦ, ἀέρος, ὕδατος, γῆς, πυρὸς
source_issues.issue: The relation of substantival μόνοις to the following element genitives is compressed. The main rendering understands things belonging only to those elements, preserving every supplied element and the only restriction; no conjectural replacement is adopted.

passages.text: This is the mystery of the sevenfold order. For he himself is the rest of all things, so that to those who imitate his greatness on a small scale he grants himself as rest. He alone is in one respect graspable and in another ungraspable, in one respect bounded and in another unbounded, having the extensions from him reaching into infinity. For he is graspable and ungraspable, near and far, being here and there, existing alone and possessing the communicating presence of the mind that is infinite on every side. By breathing this, the souls of all have life. Even if they are separated from the body, if they are found to possess longing for him, they are carried immortal into his embrace, just as in winter the vapors of the mountains, drawn by the sun’s rays, are carried toward the sun. What affection, then, can we conceive if we behold the beauty of his form with our mind? Otherwise it is impossible: for beauty cannot exist without form, nor can anyone be drawn toward love of him or even imagine seeing God if he has no form.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἑβδομάδος μυστήριον
lexical_decisions.chosen: mystery of the sevenfold order
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἑβδομάς is a group of seven or a week. Sevenfold order retains the six extensions plus rest discussed just before; mystery of the week is a viable more familiar alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ πανταχόθεν ἀπείρου νοὸς τὴν μετουσίαν ἔχων
lexical_decisions.chosen: possessing the communicating presence of the mind that is infinite on every side
lexical_decisions.rationale: μετουσία can be participation, presence, or shared influence. Communicating presence retains its life-imparting reach in the breathing clause, without silently identifying a second deity.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὸν αὐτοῦ κόλπον φέρονται
lexical_decisions.chosen: they are carried ... into his embrace
lexical_decisions.rationale: κόλπος is bosom or lap; embrace makes the intimate image readable while retaining a personal destination.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς ἐν χειμῶνι ὥρας οἱ ἀτμοὶ τῶν ὀρῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: just as in winter the vapors of the mountains
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the vapor simile and its mountain origin, without a modern scientific correction.

passages.text: But some, being strangers to the truth and allies of evil, say under the pretext of glorifying him that he is without shape, so that, being formless and without appearance, he may be visible to no one and thus not become an object of longing. For a mind that does not see God’s form is empty of him. How can someone even pray without having anyone in whom to take refuge or on whom to lean? Having nothing solid to meet it, the mind is thrown off its footing into a void. “Yes,” someone says, “one should not fear God, but love him.” I too say this. But a good conscience about every good deed will bring this about, and doing good arises from fear. “But fear,” he says, “stuns the soul.” Yet I say it does not stun it, but awakens it and turns it back. Perhaps it would rightly be said that one ought not to fear God if we human beings did not fear many other things—I mean plots from our fellows, as well as wild animals, creeping creatures, diseases, afflictions, demons, and countless other things. Let the one who demands that we not fear God rescue us from these, so that we need not fear them either. But if he cannot, why does he begrudge our being released from countless fears through one fear directed toward the just one, and becoming able through a little faith in him to remove countless afflictions from ourselves and others, while also expecting a reward of good things and, by doing no evil through fear of the God who sees everything, continuing in peace even in the present?

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀντιτυπίαν γὰρ οὐκ ἔχων εἰς κενὸν ἐκβαθρεύεται.
lexical_decisions.chosen: Having nothing solid to meet it, the mind is thrown off its footing into a void.
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀντιτυπία denotes resistance or solidity encountered; the spatial image of a supportless mind is retained rather than a modern psychological diagnosis.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐξυπνίζει καὶ ἐπιστρέφει
lexical_decisions.chosen: awakens it and turns it back
lexical_decisions.rationale: The turning verb is kept distinct from the reorientation terminology for μετανοέω.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: βραχείᾳ τῇ πρὸς αὐτὸν πίστει
lexical_decisions.chosen: through a little faith in him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the small/little qualification instead of adding great faith.

passages.text: Thus grateful servitude to the true master sets all the rest free. So if it is possible for someone not to sin without fearing God, let him not fear. For it is possible, through love for him, not to do what does not meet with his approval. For both fearing him is written and loving him is commanded, so that each person may use a medicine suited to his own constitution. One can therefore fear him because he is just. Whether you fear or love, then, do not sin. May someone who fears be able to master unlawful pleasures, not desire what belongs to others, practice love of humanity, exercise self-control, and act justly. For I see some whose fear of him is incomplete committing very many sins. Let us therefore fear God not only because he is just: for in mercy toward those who have been wronged he punishes those who have wronged them. As water extinguishes fire, so fear does away with desire for evils. The person who teaches fearlessness does not himself fear; and the person who does not fear does not believe that there will be a judgment, increases his desires, practices magic, and slanders others for the things he himself does.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ πρὸς τὸν ὄντως δεσπότην εὐγνώμων δουλεία
lexical_decisions.chosen: grateful servitude to the true master
lexical_decisions.rationale: δουλεία denotes bonded service or slavery. Servitude retains the paradox that subjection to the true master frees from other masters; grateful also allows well-disposed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς λοιποὺς πάντας ἐλευθέρους τίθησιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: sets all the rest free
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the plural all the rest; the scope may be everyone else affected or all remaining people, rather than silently replacing it with a different direct object such as all fears.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸς τὴν αὐτοῦ ἕκαστος κρᾶσιν ἐπιτηδείῳ χρήσηται φαρμάκῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: may use a medicine suited to his own constitution
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the medicine/constitution analogy and different appropriate responses rather than deleting fear or love.

passages.text: Hearing this, Simon interrupted and said, “I know whom you are addressing with these things. But so that I do not myself spend time on things I do not wish by saying the same things to refute you, you promised to answer the matters set before us. You said that you had adequately understood your teacher’s teachings because you were present to see him by direct perception and hear him, and that no one else could have the like through a vision or an apparition. But I will show that this is false. Someone who hears a person directly is not entirely assured about what is said, for his mind can reason: perhaps the figure before me, being human, is lying. An apparition, however, as soon as it is seen, gives the one seeing it assurance that it belongs to divinity. Answer me about this first.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁράματι ἢ ὀπτασίᾳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: a vision or an apparition
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὅραμα and ὀπτασία are kept distinguishable in this argument; direct perception represents ἐνάργεια, the opposed category.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μὴ ἄρα ψεύδεται (ἄνθρωπος ὢν) τὸ φαινόμενον.
lexical_decisions.chosen: perhaps the figure before me, being human, is lying
lexical_decisions.rationale: The neuter the appearing thing/figure is the source’s way of referring to the visible speaker, not necessarily a supernatural apparition in this clause.

passages.text: Peter said, “You proposed to speak to one point but answered another. For you proposed that someone could understand more ...... by hearing from an apparition than, indeed, from direct perception ... . But then you went on to persuade us that the person hearing from an apparition is more secure than the one hearing from direct perception itself. Indeed, this was why you asserted that you knew Jesus’ teachings more adequately than I, as someone who had heard the word from him through an apparition. Nevertheless I answer the point proposed at the beginning. Once the prophet has first given assurance that he is a prophet, he is securely believed concerning what he says directly; having first been recognized as truthful, he answers after being examined and questioned as the learner wishes. But someone who trusts an apparition, a vision, or a dream is in danger, for he does not know whom he trusts. It is possible that this is an evil demon or a deceptive spirit, pretending in its speech to be what it is not. If someone should wish to inquire who the one appearing is, the apparition can say whatever it wishes about itself. Thus, flashing like an evil being and remaining as long as it wishes, it is extinguished, without staying for the questioner’s examination as long as the questioner wanted. Someone who sees through dreams cannot even inquire about what he wishes, for the sleeper’s reasoning is not under his own control. This is why, though we desire to learn many things while awake, in a dream we ask about other things, or, without even asking, hear about things of no concern to us. On waking we are discouraged that we neither heard about nor examined what we desired to learn.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μᾶλλον δύνασθαί τινα πλεῖον νοεῖν ...... παρ’ ὀπτασίας ἀκούοντα, ἢ γὰρ παρὰ τῆς ἐναργείας ...
lexical_decisions.chosen: someone could understand more ...... by hearing from an apparition than, indeed, from direct perception ...
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly six and three printed gap dots remain. The comparison is retained with γάρ represented by indeed in the interrupted construction; no missing wording is restored.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δύναται λέγειν ἑαυτῷ ὃ βούλεται.
lexical_decisions.chosen: the apparition can say whatever it wishes about itself
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes the identity question as context for its self-description. The reflexive can be rendered for itself more literally; the unrestricted claim does not establish that the self-description is true.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἢ δαίμονα κακὸν εἶναι ἢ πνεῦμα πλάνον
lexical_decisions.chosen: an evil demon or a deceptive spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both alternatives remain distinct.

source_issues.source_quote: μᾶλλον δύνασθαί τινα πλεῖον νοεῖν ...... παρ’ ὀπτασίας ἀκούοντα, ἢ γὰρ παρὰ τῆς ἐναργείας ...
source_issues.issue: Six dots and then three dots mark two printed gaps. Both exact counts remain, without restoring the missing wording or hiding the interrupted syntax.

passages.text: Simon said, “If you say that apparitions do not always speak truth, nevertheless visions and dreams, being sent by God, do not lie about whatever he wishes to say.” Peter said, “You said correctly that, being sent by God, they do not lie. But it is unclear whether the person who saw it has seen a God-sent dream.” Simon said, “If the person who saw it is righteous, he has seen something true.” Peter said, “You said correctly. But who is righteous if he needs a vision to learn what he ought to learn and to do what he ought to do?” Simon said, “Grant me this, that only the righteous person can see a true vision, and I will answer you on that point. For I have decided that an impious person does not see a true dream.” Peter said, “This is false, and I can demonstrate it both without writing and from writing, though I do not promise to persuade you. For a man who has inclined toward love of a wicked woman does not transfer his mind to lawful life together with another who is good in every way. Sometimes, even knowing in themselves which is better, because they are already captivated they love the worse one. You too are suffering something like this without knowing it.” Simon said, “Leave these things aside and speak to what you promised. For it seems impossible to me for impious people to be given dreams by God in any manner.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀγράφως καὶ ἐγγράφως
lexical_decisions.chosen: both without writing and from writing
lexical_decisions.rationale: The contrast is between proof apart from written texts and proof from them, not between illiteracy and literacy.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: προειλημμένοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: because they are already captivated
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preoccupation or prior capture explains the persistence in an inferior attachment; no explicit compulsion beyond the source is added.

passages.text: Peter said, “I remember that I promised to show this and supply proof both without writing and from writing. Now listen as I speak. We know many people—if you are fair-minded; in any case I have those present as judges—who revere idols, commit adultery, and sin in every way, yet see visions and true dreams, some even apparitions of demons. For I do not say that anyone can see the fleshless form of Father or Son, because mortal eyes are dazzled by the greatest light. Therefore God’s not being seen by the human being who has been turned into flesh is not because he begrudges it, but because he is merciful. For the one who sees cannot live. The excess of light dissolves the flesh of the viewer, unless by God’s ineffable power the flesh is transformed into the nature of light so that it can see light, or the substance of light is transformed into flesh so that it can be seen by flesh. For seeing the Father without transformation belongs to the Son alone. The righteous do not see in the same way: at the resurrection of the dead, when their bodies have been transformed into light and they become equal to angels, then they will be able to see. Indeed, even if one of the angels attempts to appear to a human being, he turns into flesh so that he can be seen by flesh. For no one can see a fleshless power, not only that of the Son but not even that of an angel. But if someone sees an apparition, let him understand it to be that of an evil demon.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν γὰρ ἄσαρκον ἰδέαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the fleshless form
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains form without flesh, not shapelessness, since the argument distinguishes the two.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ εἰς σάρκα τετραμμένῳ ἀνθρώπῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: the human being who has been turned into flesh
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the transformation wording without replacing it with a philosophical assumption about human origins.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ γὰρ ἀτρέπτως πατέρα ἰδεῖν υἱοῦ μόνου ἐστίν.
lexical_decisions.chosen: For seeing the Father without transformation belongs to the Son alone.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Without transformation can concern the conditions of the seeing encounter or the viewer/seen; English leaves the qualification unassigned rather than claiming explicitly which party remains unchanged.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἰσάγγελοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: equal to angels
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains equality to angels, not an assertion that human beings become angels.

passages.text: Nevertheless, that even impious people see true visions and dreams is clear, and I can prove it from writing. For it is written in the law that Abimelech—being impious and having wished to defile the wife of righteous Abraham through intercourse—heard from God in sleep, as the scripture says, not to touch her because she was living with a husband. Pharaoh too, an impious man, saw a dream about abundance and scarcity of wheat; Joseph, explaining it to him, said that the dream had come from God. Nebuchadnezzar, who revered idols and ordered those who revered God to be thrown into fire, saw a dream concerning an age’s whole length. And let no one say, “But no impious person beholds a vision while awake.” That is false. Nebuchadnezzar himself, after ordering three men to be thrown into fire, looked into the furnace and spoke of a fourth: “I see the fourth as a son of God.” Yet although they saw true apparitions, visions, and dreams, they were impious. Such a person is not necessarily reverent simply because he sees visions, dreams, and apparitions. For to the reverent person truth wells up in an inborn and pure mind, not pursued through a dream, but given to good people through understanding.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν τέταρτον ὁρῶ ὡς υἱὸν θεοῦ
lexical_decisions.chosen: I see the fourth as a son of God
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the anarthrous son of God in the quoted statement without identifying the figure as a particular later doctrinal person.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὄνειρον ὅλου μήκους αἰῶνος
lexical_decisions.chosen: a dream concerning an age’s whole length
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the broad age-duration wording rather than identifying an unprinted historical timetable.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ γὰρ εὐσεβεῖ ἐμφύτῳ καὶ καθαρῷ ἀναβλύζει τῷ νῷ τὸ ἀληθές
lexical_decisions.chosen: to the reverent person truth wells up in an inborn and pure mind
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adjectival grouping can also be taken as in the reverent, inborn, and pure mind; both emphasize inward truth and do not make the dream the source of it.

passages.text: For this is how the Son was revealed to me too by the Father. Therefore I know the power of revelation, having learned from my own experience. For as soon as the Lord asked who people said he was, and I had heard different people saying different things about him, it rose in my heart. I do not know, then, how I said, “You are the Son of the living God.” He pronounced me blessed and told me that the one who had revealed it was the Father. From then on I learned that learning without being taught, without an apparition or dreams, is revelation. And this truly is so. For in the thing placed within us by God in seed form ...., all truth resides. It is covered and uncovered by God’s hand, the one who brings this about knowing what accords with each person’s worth. But that something is made known from outside through apparitions and dreams is plainly not a matter of revelation but of anger. Indeed, it is written in the law that God, angry with Aaron and Miriam, said, “If a prophet arises from among you, through visions and dreams I will make myself known to him; but not in this way as with Moses my servant, because I will speak to him in visible form and not through dreams, as someone will speak to his own friend.” You see how the things of anger come through visions and dreams, whereas those addressed to a friend are mouth to mouth, in visible form, and not through riddles, visions, and dreams as to an enemy.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἐν ἡμῖν ἐκ θεοῦ τεθείσῃ σπερματικῶς....
lexical_decisions.chosen: For in the thing placed within us by God in seed form ....
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly four gap dots remain. Thing is generic English nominal support for the surviving article/participle; it does not identify the unavailable noun or restore a specific faculty.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: θεοῦ δὲ χειρὶ σκέπεται καὶ ἀποκαλύπτεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: It is covered and uncovered by God’s hand
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the cover/uncover opposition underlying revelation rather than describing only disclosure.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Μωϋσῇ τῷ θεράποντί μου
lexical_decisions.chosen: Moses my servant
lexical_decisions.rationale: θεράπων is an attendant or servant; the wording is retained without importing a different familiar biblical quotation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν εἴδει
lexical_decisions.chosen: in visible form
lexical_decisions.rationale: εἶδος is appearance or form, fitting the contrast with dream and riddle. Directly is a looser alternative that would obscure the explicit form-language.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἐν ἡμῖν ἐκ θεοῦ τεθείσῃ σπερματικῶς....
source_issues.issue: The four-dot printed gap leaves a noun or additional wording unavailable. Exactly four dots remain, and thing is only generic English grammatical support, not an identification or recovery of the lost content.

passages.text: If, then, our Jesus also appeared to you through a vision, was made known, and conversed with you, it was as with an adversary, in anger. That is why he spoke through visions and dreams, or even through revelations that come from outside. But can anyone become wise for teaching through an apparition? If you say, “It is possible,” why did the teacher remain and converse with people who were awake for an entire year? And how shall we even believe you about the very claim that he appeared to you? How did he appear to you, when you think the opposite of his teaching? But if, after being seen and instructed by him for a single hour, you became an apostle, proclaim his words, explain his teachings, love his apostles, and do not fight me, who lived with him. For you have stood against me as an enemy, when I am a solid rock, a foundation of an assembly. If you were not an adversary, you would not, by slandering me, revile the proclamation that comes through me, so that I should not be believed when I say what I myself heard from the Lord while present—as though I had clearly been condemned and were unapproved. Or if you call me “condemned,” you accuse the God who revealed the Messiah to me and attack the one who pronounced me blessed on account of revelation. But if you truly wish to cooperate with the truth, first learn from us what we learned from him, and, becoming a disciple of truth, become our fellow worker.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπ’ ἐκείνου μιᾶς ὥρας ὀφθεὶς καὶ μαθητευθεὶς
lexical_decisions.chosen: after being seen and instructed by him for a single hour
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the passive being seen by him rather than silently reversing it into seeing him. The hour qualifies the short encounter and instruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: στερεὰν πέτραν ὄντα με, θεμέλιον ἐκκλησίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: when I am a solid rock, a foundation of an assembly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Peter’s self-description as rock/foundation. Church is a conventional alternative for ἐκκλησία, but the Greek does not specify a later institution.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν χριστὸν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses the POB title rendering because χριστός here functions independently, not in a personal-name construction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: „κατεγνωσμένον“
lexical_decisions.chosen: “condemned”
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the marked quoted verdict without identifying an unnamed opponent with a historical person not named in this section.

passages.text: Hearing this, Simon said, “Far be it from me to become a disciple either of him or of you. For I am not ignorant of what must be known. What I asked about as though learning was so that I might know whether you can show direct perception to be more evident than an apparition. But you said what you wished; you did not demonstrate it. And now, tomorrow, I will come and speak with you on the subject of God, whom you insist is the maker, and show that he is not the highest and good. I will also show that your teacher said the same things as I, and expose you as not having understood.” After saying this, he went out, unwilling to hear an answer to the matters he had proposed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὀπτασίας ἐνάργειαν ἐναργεστέραν δεῖξαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: show direct perception to be more evident than an apparition
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the repeated evidence/evident wording and the comparison of apparition with direct experience.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μὴ αὐτὸν εἶναι ἀνώτατον καὶ ἀγαθόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: that he is not the highest and good
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the coordinated predicate under the negative without silently splitting it into two independent categorical denials.
